text:
ashley: Heads up — CI flagged a promptset ancestry/provenance mismatch for the new spanish-qa fixture set. failing early in eval-runner because lineage_id is missing :thinking_face:

mike: ugh. which job? link?

ashley: eval-ci:run-42 on master. trunk failure: `holdout-bleed-check` step. gist of the log: `Detected related_shard present but no provenance.metadata.ancestry_id`

mike: can you paste the exact log lines?

ashley: sure:
```
ERROR eval.runner.holdout - holdout-bleed-check failed for promptset spanish-qa-v2
reason=MissingProvenance: expected ancestry_id for fixture cohort 'spanish-qa' but none found
related_shard=shard-2026-03-19-4
```

sara: is this the synthetic generated set or imported?

ashley: imported from partner dump, then we ran the synthetic augmentation job. looks like the import preserved `related_shard` but dropped `provenance` fields in the augmentation step.

kevin: that explains it — our augment pipeline has a legacy transformer that reconstructs records and currently drops `provenance.*`. i'll open a quick PR to preserve `provenance`.

olivia: for triage: this is causing holdout gating to skip on some runs (false positives) or fail depending on strictness. either way, it blocks canary bring-up for the spanish model. cc @mike on release impact.

mike: thanks. can we add a CI guard that fails early if a promptset has `related_shard` without `provenance.ancestry_id`? cheap fix.

kevin: yep. plan: 1) hotfix augmenter to copy provenance through, 2) add a lint check in eval CI (holdout-bleed-check preflight) to assert provenance when related_shard present, 3) minor data migration to backfill for existing imported sets.

ashley: migrating existing sets — do we have a safe canonical source for ancestry ids? partner provided a manifest with `ancestry_catalog.csv` in the raw bucket. i can write a backfill script that matches on shard id to restore ancestry_id.

mike: do that. also let's add a lightweight verification step to the backfill that runs the holdout-bleed-check locally on a sample shard before committing. saves us a second round.

kevin: PR incoming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/augmenter/pull/382 (hotfix preserves provenance). tests included.

eval-ci-bot: build 382 passed unit + integration. but full eval CI still failing on `holdout-bleed-check` for spanish-qa-v2 (same error) — looks like backfill needed.

olivia: ashley, can you run the backfill for the specific failing shard and paste the command?

ashley: running now: 
```bash
$ python tools/backfill_provenance.py --bucket gs://redwood-imports/partnerX --shard shard-2026-03-19-4 --dry-run
Found manifest entry: shard-2026-03-19-4 -> ancestry_id=anc-7734
Dry-run: would update 124 records.
```

ashley: running actual backfill in 2m. will post when finished.

(6 minutes later)

ashley: backfill complete. updated 124 records. restarted eval-CI for that branch.

eval-ci-bot: retriggered job eval-ci:run-42. new run shows `holdout-bleed-check` passed for spanish-qa-v2 :white_check_mark:

mike: excellent. next: ensure augmenter unit tests check provenance passthrough and add a small e2e that simulates import+augment+eval so this doesn't regress.

kevin: adding tests now. also adding a short note to the promptset onboarding doc about mandatory metadata keys: `provenance.ancestry_id`, `provenance.ingest_time`, and `related_shard` usage.

olivia: can someone add a postmortem-lite in eng-ml/retrospectives so product knows why spanish canary got delayed? 2-3 bullets is fine.

ashley: will write a quick summary.

mike: nice catch. small ask for future: if augment pipeline touches prompt IDs, add an `x-original-id` header so provenance is obvious.

kevin: agree. will include that in the PR.

olivia: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
